source_title: The Mirage Breaks, and the Script Turns Eschatological
summary: This Dialogue Works interview extends Strategy and Eschatology by making the first week of the Iran war a live test of ground-troop escalation, Hormuz as world-system nexus, Gulf mirage fragility, and Jiang's explicit break from ordinary history into end-times script analysis.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Hormuz is treated as the nexus of global trade where oil flows, Asian economies, Russia, China, Europe, and American imperial survival meet.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The source directly reprises the Strategy page's systems-pivot anchor: the strait is not local geography but the place where energy, trade, reserve order, and military credibility become one board.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Ground troops turn the war into World War III, while retreat or visible defeat threatens the empire's protection story.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The interview gives a first-week live-war version of the no-exit trap: airpower preserves fantasy, ground troops create irreversible commitment, and even defeat is read as potentially part of the larger script.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: The Gulf bargain runs through royal protection, petrodollar recycling, American bases, and now AI/data-center finance.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The passage supports Power As Alchemy when the active object is the monetary-protection bargain that makes Gulf wealth, U.S. finance, and platform investment feel stable.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Jiang says ordinary strategic and historical frameworks fail because actors are trying to bring about a divine world through Al-Aqsa, the Third Temple, and the second coming of Jesus.
existing_lens_links.rationale: The source directly strengthens the Eschatology page's promise-becomes-plan mechanism: prophecy is treated as an operational sequence rather than decorative belief.

existing_lens_links.episode_phrase: Jiang moves from nation-state actors to hidden entities above nation-states and asks who is behind the curtain pulling the strings.
existing_lens_links.rationale: This belongs to Secret Society only when the active mechanism is hidden coordination above public state actors; the eschatological script remains the reason the hidden pressure can feel coherent.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use this 2026-03-07 Dialogue Works interview as the earliest first-week live-war Strategy pressure after the war begins: ground troops are named as the irreversible World War III threshold, Hormuz is the world-system nexus, the Gulf mirage depends on desalination/imported labor/foreign protection, and proxy invasion is framed as cannon fodder plus grift rather than a serious liberation route.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Strategy owns troops, chokepoints, infrastructure fragility, proxy feasibility, and war-exit costs. Power As Alchemy owns the petrodollar/protection loop; Eschatology owns Jiang's later claim that ordinary strategy no longer explains the war.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Add this source as a sharper March 7 live-war escalation of the Israel-Iran end-times sequence: Jiang explicitly says history and ordinary geopolitics can no longer explain the war, names the framework as eschatological-religious, and connects Trump, Al-Aqsa, the Third Temple, Christian Zionist return-of-Jesus belief, and possible world-war acceleration.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Eschatology owns sacred role-script causality and the methodological switch away from ordinary history. Strategy still owns whether tactical nuclear use, ground invasion, and Russian cover are materially executable.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the Gulf-devil's-bargain sequence as supporting evidence for the dollar-protection loop: Gulf monarchies trade obedience and petrodollar recycling for protection, while bases protect ruling families and U.S. financial/AI bubbles more than local populations.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Power As Alchemy owns the protection belief and recycling loop. Strategy owns the wartime audit that reveals the loop cannot physically protect the Gulf.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Hold the behind-the-curtain passages as attributed, high-uncertainty evidence for the hidden-coordination boundary: Jiang explicitly questions nation-states as the main unit, names possible organizations above states, and ends by saying the real war is to understand who is pulling strings.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Secret Society owns hidden coordination and above-state agency only when the claim remains visibly attributed and uncertainty-preserved. Eschatology owns the sacred script; Game Theory owns visible player payoffs.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use the closing 'war of self-knowledge' only if the page is already being revised: Jiang says focusing on U.S.-Iran battlefield prediction may itself be the desired attention frame, while the real task is seeing who is behind the curtain.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Attention Capture owns the misdirection and self-knowledge frame. Secret Society owns the behind-the-curtain agency claim; Strategy owns the invasion-force prediction.

chronology_notes.note: The source is recorded on 2026-03-07, one week into the Iran war, and should be treated as a first-week live-war formulation before later March 9, March 12, March 20, and March 24 recurrences sharpen the no-exit and escalation-ladder frames.

The interview preserves Jiang's early-war distinction between airpower and ground troops: air campaigns can preserve the fantasy of exit, while ground troops make the conflict irreversible and world-war-scaled.

Live-war reports about Azerbaijan, Saudi facilities, Qatar, Omani mediation, tactical nuclear possibilities, and false flags must remain dated and attributed to Jiang's March 7 wartime frame rather than normalized into settled public chronology.

The source marks Jiang's strongest methodological break in the March war cluster: after arguing from Hormuz, empire, Gulf infrastructure, and proxy feasibility, he says the traditional understanding of wars cannot be used anymore and switches to an eschatological-religious framework.

The closing prediction that the United States will invade Iran and Iran will destroy the invasion force is immediately reframed by Jiang as a possible distraction from the deeper question of hidden agency and self-knowledge.

next_actions.action: Before adding this source to public Strategy prose, run a concept-scoped compression/review of the March 2026 Iran-war cluster; the Strategy page already has multiple March recurrences, so this source is most valuable as the first-week chronology and Gulf-mirage/ground-troop formulation rather than another full section.

A later Eschatology pass should compare the March 7 methodological break against the March 9 Sneako and George Galloway formulations, preserving that this interview moves from ordinary strategy into eschatology inside the same conversation.
